rationale: The 2026.11.3 deploy raised WORKER_CONCURRENCY from 8 to 32 (LOG-0001-0006); 32 workers started (LOG-0001-0007) against an orders-db pool still capped at 20 connections (LOG-0001-0008). The pool then saturated with requests waiting (LOG-0001-0016) and requests began timing out while acquiring a connection (LOG-0001-0023). Reverting the concurrency change ends the incident, so by the trigger rule the category is config_or_deploy_change, not resource_exhaustion. Supporting: the pool was lightly used before the deploy (LOG-0001-0003); the cache-miss spike recovered before the latency rose (LOG-0001-0014), so it is a red herring; the database itself had spare sessions and low CPU (LOG-0001-0025, LOG-0001-0034); the later saturation, timeouts, 503s, SLO breach and the ticket show the same mechanism and its impact.

From 00:00:04 every payments-worker call to ledger-gateway.internal.example fails with 'TLS handshake failed: certificate has expired' (LOG-0002-0010), and the peer certificate's not_after is 2026-11-12T00:00:00Z (LOG-0002-0016): the upstream's certificate expired at midnight. Renewing it ends the incident, so the category is expired_credential. Supporting: the renewal job had failed DNS validation and given up two days earlier (LOG-0002-0001 to 0003), which explains why it expired; the repeated handshake failures, dead-lettered batches, 97% error rate and growing queues are the impact; the GC pauses (LOG-0002-0007, LOG-0002-0021) are minor and unrelated, and the health checks passed because they do not exercise the upstream.
